questions.question: A face shield should:

options.text: Give you a clear view to both sides.
Block all air from passing through it.
Be tight enough so glasses cannot fit under it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give you a clear view to both sides.
questions.explanation: A good face shield must have no scratches, resist damage, give clear views to both sides, fasten securely, let air pass through, and have room for eyeglasses or sunglasses if needed.

questions.question: A proper lane position should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Help you see and be seen better.
Show other drivers what you plan to do.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help you avoid traffic signals.
questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you see others and be seen. It helps you avoid wind blasts, other drivers' blind spots, and road hazards. Your position should stop other drivers from sharing your lane and give you an escape route if danger appears.

questions.question: It is important to flash your brake light when:

options.text: You will slow down where other drivers do not expect it.
There is a stop sign ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: You will slow down where other drivers do not expect it.
questions.explanation: Motorcycle brake lights are harder to see than car brake lights. Flashing your brake light helps other drivers notice it. Flash your brake light before you slow down where drivers may not expect it, such as in the middle of a block or near an alley.

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:
questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs that show road rules, like speed limits, are usually rectangular with white background and black text or symbols. You must follow the rules shown on these signs.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle:

options.text: You may ride on the shoulder.
You may finish the pass in a no passing zone.
You must start and finish the pass in a passing zone.
You should honk your horn to make the other driver slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must start and finish the pass in a passing zone.
questions.explanation: All passing must happen within the speed limit and only where it is safe and legal to pass.

questions.question: If your motorcycle starts to wobble, you should:

options.text: Hold the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle.
questions.explanation: Do not speed up during a wobble because it will make the motorcycle less stable. Instead, hold the handlebars firmly, slow down by gently closing the throttle, move your weight forward and down, and pull off the road as soon as possible. Do not brake, as this can make the wobble worse.

questions.question: To reduce your chances of a crash, you should:

options.text: Use your turn signals when you plan to change lanes.
Look only 15 feet ahead of your motorcycle.
Not use your headlight during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your turn signals when you plan to change lanes.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, you should be visible, tell other drivers your plans, keep safe distances, look at least 12 seconds ahead, spot and avoid hazards, and be ready for changes in road conditions.

questions.question: To stay in control while turning your motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Speed up before you enter the turn.
Look through the turn to see what is ahead.
Come to a complete stop before entering the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look through the turn to see what is ahead.
questions.explanation: To stay in control through a turn, look through the turn by turning only your head. Slow down before the turn and lean your motorcycle in the right direction.

questions.question: Reflective clothing should:

options.text: Be worn only during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be worn day and night.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen in daylight. Wearing bright colors and reflective materials at all times makes you more visible and safer.

questions.question: Which clothing item will not reduce crash injuries?
questions.correctAnswerText: Shorts
questions.explanation: To reduce injury, wear a helmet, eye protection, heavy shoes or boots, full-length pants, a jacket, and full-fingered gloves. Choose durable materials for the best protection.

questions.question: A windshield:

options.text: Works as well as a face shield.
Does not fully protect your eyes from wind.
Should be used only on windy days.

questions.correctAnswerText: Does not fully protect your eyes from wind.
questions.explanation: A windshield is not the same as goggles or a face shield. Most windshields will not protect your eyes from the wind.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Always stay away from the left side of the lane.
Always stay away from the right side of the lane.
Always stay away from the center of the lane.
Use whichever part of the lane is safest.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use whichever part of the lane is safest.
questions.explanation: There is no one part of the lane you should always avoid. Change your position based on road conditions.

questions.question: More than half of all crashes:
questions.correctAnswerText: Involve inexperienced riders.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes involve riders who are new to their motorcycle.

questions.question: After drinking, what reduces the effects of alcohol?
questions.correctAnswerText: Time
questions.explanation: Your liver removes alcohol at a fixed rate. Nothing can speed this up. Only time will lessen alcohol's effects on your body.

questions.question: When braking, you should:

options.text: Squeeze the front brake and press the rear brake.
Grab the front brake and squeeze the rear brake.
Push hard on the front brake and grab the rear brake.
Press the front brake and push hard on the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Squeeze the front brake and press the rear brake.
questions.explanation: To brake, squeeze the front brake lever and press down on the rear brake pedal. Always use both brakes when slowing or stopping.

questions.question: A motorcyclist is well-protected if they are wearing:

options.text: A jacket that leaves the arms exposed.
Shoes that do not cover the ankle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leather gloves.
questions.explanation: For protection, wear a jacket and pants that cover your arms and legs fully. Boots or shoes should be tall and strong enough to cover and support your ankles. Footwear should have low heels that will not catch on foot pegs. Leather gloves protect your hands in a crash and give you a better grip on the controls.

questions.question: To reduce your chance of crashing, you should:

options.text: Skip using your turn signal when changing lanes.
Look only five feet ahead while riding.
Always be ready to use crash-avoidance moves.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always be ready to use crash-avoidance moves.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, make sure others can see you. Use your signals, brake light, and lane position to show your intentions. Keep space around your motorcycle and watch the road ahead, behind, and to the side. Always be ready to avoid an unexpected hazard.

questions.question: A shatter-resistant face shield:

options.text: Can protect a rider's face during a crash.
Does not protect as much as goggles.
Should not be worn with a helmet.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can protect a rider's face during a crash.
questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face in a crash. Goggles protect only your eyes, not your whole face. A face shield also protects you from dirt, dust, insects, rain, and small rocks.

questions.question: If your motorcycle starts to wobble, you should:

options.text: Grip the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Grip the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle.
questions.explanation: Do not speed up because this will make the wobble worse. Instead, grip the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle to slow down. Lean forward and down, then pull off the road as soon as you can. Do not use the brakes, as this may make the wobble worse.

questions.question: The center portion of a lane:

options.text: Is always the best place for a motorcycle to ride.
Has oil and grease, but is usually safe for riding.
Has oil and grease, and is never safe for riding.
Is the smoothest part of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Has oil and grease, but is usually safe for riding.
questions.explanation: Oil from cars drips onto the center of each lane. On dry roads, this area usually has enough traction for motorcycles to ride safely. Avoid heavy buildups of oil and grease, which are common at busy intersections and toll booths.

questions.question: Where is the throttle usually located?
questions.correctAnswerText: On the right handle grip
questions.explanation: The throttle is on the right handle grip. Learn where all your motorcycle's controls are before you ride.

questions.question: How often should a motorcycle rider check their mirrors?

options.text: More often than the time spent looking ahead

questions.correctAnswerText: Frequently
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often to watch for hazards behind you.

questions.question: Which should you NOT do to stay safe when riding at night?

options.text: Use your high beam headlight when possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase your speed.
questions.explanation: To ride safely at night, slow down, use your high beam when no other vehicles are near, and stay farther back from the vehicle ahead. Watch vehicles in front of you for clues about the road. Their headlights and taillights help you see what is coming.

questions.question: A rider wearing a helmet is _______ more likely to survive a crash than a rider without a helmet.
questions.correctAnswerText: Three times
questions.explanation: Riders without helmets are three times more likely to die from head injuries in a crash than riders who wear helmets.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead.
